The game mechanics differ from the demo and thus I can no longer recommend the game. In the demo, to unlock new items you gathered "souls". These were received through progressing as far through each run as you can, as well as taking additional risk on killing as many enemies as possible per stage. Unlocking one character would take multiple runs. In the release, you unlock items by earning shards gained through steam achievements. This creates an initial burst of progress (I unlocked every single character and half a dozen emblems in the first run, which would have taken many hours in the demo) and then stalls until you unlock further achievements.

So, this game was released by the Yogscast alongside a game called Border Pioneer. Border Pioneer turned out to just be an unfinished re-skin of an existing Chinese game. It has a medieval European visual theme, sort of, with Chinese music. The UI even bugs out from time to time revealing all the original Chinese text. Anyway, my guess is that this game is more of the same. It seems like the re-skinning process went a little more smoothly with this one, but maybe that's just because there was a lot less to re-skin. Nothing wrong with any of that in principle, but just realize that these aren't games that Lewis and Simon fell in love with while playing or helped to create. They're just games that they think they can sell under their branding for more money than they paid to buy and re-skin them. All that having been said, this game is pretty average. 5/10. It functions well enough as a roguelite, but it doesn't really bring anything new or exciting to the table. There's a real lack of character past the introduction, and you fight the same things in the same order with small variations every run. There's very limited narration or theming past the immediate visuals, making this game narratively dry. The market is saturated at this point, so I don't know why anyone would want play this mediocre cash grab when there are literally dozens of excellent roguelites out there to choose from. Also, gating progress behind hidden steam achievements is a wild decision. Don't do that.

食之无味，弃之可惜。不建议现在入手，你找个主播看一遍通关就是这个游戏的全部了。 拿一个最简单的角度出发，这类游戏应该最起码有三个流派：高攻、高防、道具 但是游玩下来只有高攻能打，是所有角色，所有道具，所有策略最后都要落脚在加攻上，实在是没意思，设计这么多遗物也挺累吧，感觉开发者也不需要花心思设计了，你就留个长矛干杯算了。这在我看来是很严重的问题，作为消费者所有角色，所有对局体验下来一摸一样，通关一次后再打感到一种极其无趣的重复感，没有游玩下去的欲望，也完全对不起这个价位。 此外还有让我备感疑惑的一点，游戏里面的局外购买能不能再提示的明显一点，我打了很久还发现我咋啥徽章没解锁，最后才在图鉴里看见要买，挺莫名其妙的小问题，适当提醒一下可以改善大家的体验。 虽然现在游戏的框架已经定下来了，我也不知道怎么才能立竿见影的解决第一个说的流派问题，但希望制作者能找到方法，让游戏更加有决策的感觉而不是无脑加一个点。 希望以后我还会打开它玩，但至少现在不会了。

在卡牌游戏百花齐放的当今，肉鸽类卡牌更是层出不穷。而本作《迷失之径》则以其独特的设计理念和独特的玩法脱颖而出，游戏所谓的结合空当接龙的玩法迅速吸引了我，毕竟小学的微机课，空当接龙和扫雷可是我最爱的两款windows自带游戏。 《迷失之径》的故事发生在一个随机生成的像素化迷失世界中，玩家将扮演风格各异技能不同的冒险家，面对充满未知的区域和危险的挑战，不断向前推进。游戏的剧情方面没有过多的描述，玩家直接便可以开启卡牌肉鸽的挑战。 [h1]独特而有趣的肉鸽卡牌玩法[/h1] 《迷失之径》的商店页面介绍说游戏结合了空当接龙与肉鸽卡牌元素，创造出一种全新的策略冒险体验，这让我非常感兴趣。一方面空当接龙对我来说非常熟悉，我小学微机课基本上就是不断的在玩空当接龙和扫雷。另一方面，我也很好奇游戏如何在空当接龙的游戏中取经，又是如何融入到肉鸽卡牌游戏里面的。 当我正式进入游戏后，游戏独特的玩法揭开了这个谜题。游戏中玩家面对每个房间都会有5个放置卡牌的空间，可能会出现敌人，也可能会出现道具和补给品，甚至通往下一个房间的选项也在其中。而卡牌永远只显示最上面的一张，下面的卡牌会被隐藏。玩家就像玩空当接龙一样，需要探索下面的卡牌内容，直到寻找到通往下一个房间的出路。玩家可以通过挪动卡牌来将暂时不想处理的卡牌挪动到其他的空位来揭开下面卡牌的内容，也可以将暂时不想使用的道具挪动到背包空格中，游戏中玩家可以挪动卡牌保存2个道具，以备不时之需。游戏的核心玩法就是利用技能与道具的组合，战胜各种敌人，探索关卡，并不断寻找破关的通路。这种机制让每一次翻开卡牌都充满未知与刺激，玩家的决策成为影响胜负的关键因素，因为玩家想不到揭开下面的一张卡牌是生命药剂帮助玩家回复生命再拼一次，还是会出现一颗炸弹，直接结束一次游戏，这种策略与运气并存的感觉，确实是空当接龙的味道，甚至在游戏更加具象化体验之后，这种感觉得到了极大的提升与升华。 此外，游戏也存在一些岔路和分支，在这个时候每张卡牌也代表一种选择，最基础的便是下一个房间的奖励，有时候玩家会掀开获得多个不同的下级房间的种类，玩家需要根据目前的状况进行选择来获得最优化的成长和提升。一些事件的分支选择，会影响接下来玩家面对的其他事件或是敌人的种类，甚至影响最终的游戏结局。玩家需要谨慎考虑每一次选择，制定出最佳策略，以应对不断变化的挑战。 [h1]角色、装备、道具与技能提升[/h1] 《迷失之径》为玩家提供了多个各具特色的角色，每个角色都有独特的技能和属性。玩家可以根据自己的喜好和策略方向选择合适的角色，并通过升级、装备道具等方式提升角色的实力。游戏的角色能力提升主要通过属性的变化，其中最直接的便是装备与技能。游戏的装备系统非常丰富多样，超过一百种装备和道具供玩家选择搭配，不同的装备与角色技能组合将产生各式各样的战斗流派，增加了游戏的可玩性和复杂性。同时游戏的装备也是可以提升等级的，花费资源提升等级可以提高装备的作用，甚至可以将其转化为永久的属性加成。玩家将在随机生成的地图中进行探索，每一次进入游戏，玩家都将面临一个全新的世界，不同的敌人、事件和奖励让每一次冒险都充满新鲜感。玩家也可以尝试挑战不同的装备与技能的组合来寻找更适合自己的通关方式。 [h1]Steam Deck游玩体验[/h1] 本作游戏的Steam Deck兼容性目前还处于未知待了解状态，不过经过我个人的测试游戏是可以在Steam Deck上面运行的。不过因为游戏有很多的拖动操作，导致使用SD的手柄操作比较麻烦，可能需要触控板和R2键的协调合作。经过我个人的体验拖动操作在长时间游玩之后会感觉很累，而且经常会有误操作出现，因此我个人不是很推荐使用SD游玩。如果未来游戏能够推出支持手柄操作的话另说，并且如果不怕麻烦，硬要使用SD游玩的玩家，也是可以在这种不舒服的状态下玩的。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]

This is the first game that's hooked me since last August. I originally didn't buy it because it doesn't have controller support, but I got a mouse for my Steam Deck so I can try some new things. Stray Path didn't immediately appeal to me—perhaps because I'm not a cat person—but it went on sale yesterday so it felt like time to give it a go. I think the game's biggest strength is its simplicity. You click to attack and the enemy retaliates if it can. You can inflict status effects, but enemies can do worse to you. You grow your stats when you find blessing alters, you get extra bonuses for clearing out stages, you collect rune stones to upgrade relics you find, and the relics are really the key to surviving a run. It took about an hour to beat for the first time on easy mode, which is about twice as fast as it usually takes. That's not to say the game doesn't pose a challenge, but that I figured out ways to exploit it almost immediately. My job involves finding exploits in systems, so I'm kind of tuned into this sort of thing every day. It does pose a unique challenge, compared to other games I've played, and I didn't feel like it was too easy—just really easy to understand. Most games take me twice as long because I don't understand how they work. I would've finished on my second run had I managed to understand why one enemy kept killing me when it didn't advertise it would. So, this is where my complaints come in. I don't understand how certain things work in the game, and I'm not sure if they're supposed to work how they do. There's one enemy in the fourth location that would basically insta-kill me if I attacked it and it had the opportunity to retaliate. Nothing on the card indicated it would do this, so I still don't understand why this happened, but I just followed a lot of cursed paths to get rare relics that generate a ton of items after one kill, used those to weaken the enemy with indirect damage, and then finished it off with a standard attack. So, in a way, it was kind of fun trying to figure out how to beat an enemy that didn't act the way its card said it would, but I think I'd still prefer things to work according to the stated rules. Also, I've unlocked most of the emblem equipped slots, but only one emblem. I've unlocked absolutely nothing else in any category, and I don't know what I'm supposed to do to unlock these things. You'd think that beating the game, even on easy mode, would unlock at least one thing but no. It's possible that the unlock conditions are somewhere in the bestiary, but I haven't gone searching for them yet. It's really weird to me that the locked slots tell you what you're going to unlock rather than the condition for unlocking it. I would much rather be surprised by the reward then not know how to gain the reward. All of my complaints about Stray Path have to do with missing information. I'm sure there are a few things I just missed because I sometimes rush my way through things and often ignore instructions in favor of just figuring out how to play on my own, but Stray Path has an unusually good and short tutorial, and you're forced to do it properly, so I actually paid attention. I'm going to just look up how some of these things work, but I don't think a game should put you in a position where you have to go elsewhere for information that could be easily provided in the game. All of that said, this is a really fun game. I realize I complained about issues than I complimented the game, but I really enjoyed it and want to play it more, but I'm getting tripped up because of the issues. But to even things out I'm going to try and articulate the good stuff (besides how easy it is to learn). I think one of the things I really liked was the amount of control the game provides you. While your options dwindle as you go on, for half the run you pretty much have the ability to choose the paths that contain what you need as you proceed to the next stage. If you need rune stones, you can choose rune stones. If you have at least five rune stones, you can safely choose the relic upgrade path and not miss out on anything. The game doesn't give you a ton of relics right away, so they're easy to manage and keep upgraded. You don't have to make any hard choices right away as you figure out your approach to the game based on what you find. I really like this. Wildfrost, which is my favorite, does not do you any favors like this and it's my one complaint about the game. I spent a year breaking that game completely, so I don't ever lose, but some runs are just annoying because the RNG isn't balanced. Stray Path does a great job of giving you the opportunity to always find what you need without too much trouble, and it's your mistake if you don't make the best of it. I appreciate this a lot, because you never feel like it's preventing you from enjoying your run. As with most roguelike/roguelite games, it's the artifacts/relics/bonuses/upgrades/etc., and the synergies you can create between them, that makes them fun. Stray Path allows for some really interesting synergies. Earlier, I mentioned the card generator relics. These are fairly easy to get if you follow enough cursed paths and/or can afford rare chests. Items aren't always very useful, but lots of items exploit the game in a fun way. As soon as you have your first kill, if you have three upgraded item-generating relics, six cards just get spammed out and cover up enemies. So, you not only get lots of helpful stuff to use, but you can pick off enemies solo more easily. In the later stages, this is super useful because enemies synergize with each other. You can also exploit relic abilities in fun ways. There's one, whose name I forget, that stacks damage on items in your inventory every time you attack or use an item. Leave a bomb in your inventory for several stage and you can one shot every boss (except for the final one, though this tactic is still very useful in that fight). So, if this kind of stuff appeals to you, you'll probably enjoy Stray Path. I just wish I could figure out how to increase the difficulty and unlock more things. :-P There's so much more game I can't play without knowing that... ***** UPDATE: I am an idiot. Unlocks happen in the beastiary and there's a giant arrow with text that says "UNLOCK" bouncing up and down on the main screen. I have an unusual talent for looking everywhere something is not. So, I my complaint about that is not valid. :-p

The game is nice and has good ideas, I like the concept and the character art. Sadly all characters play the same until you make the game very hard. This is when you get effects that are unique to the different characters. I like the idea that higher difficulty unlocks more abilities, but the fist ability gets unlocked at very high difficulty and the second at nightmare difficulty. So unless you play like that all characters feel exactly the same. The game also feels kind of imbalanced and punishing. Once you get to a cartain level most enemys are trivial, until you miss a detail and are dead. 90% of my deaths were not because of an enemy being too tough or countering me, but because I klicked too fast and oversaw some ability of another enemy - this is really frustrating. Maybe a "restart room" option when you die would be nice. For these reasons I do not recommend this game altough i like the concept and art.

Buy Ring of Pain, not this game. I tried giving it a chance, but it's just not good. The ideas are there, but they're all half-baked. All unlocks are tied to achievements, which may seem okay at first, but they can be more and more difficult to achieve later on - this means even if you have an incredible, op build going that gets you far, you may eventually die and get no currency to unlock more characters, emblems, or items. Indicators exist to show what will happen when you attack a specific enemy, but not what other untargeted enemies will do. Late game, the "difficulty" simply lies in the fact that most enemies deal unblockable damage - that's not a fun mechanic, it's just lazy, uninspired artificial difficulty. Audio is severely. There are only 1-2 audio tracks, a few sound effects, and many times actions result in no sound at all when it really seems like you should be hearing something. You'll find yourself playing nearly the same way every run. While the characters are different enough on paper, you come across class-specific trinkets so rarely that you don't often get to experience meaningful differences. Given that the game is 8 months old and exists as it does in its current state, it doesn't seem like it's going to evolve into anything spectacular. I'm willing to try it again if the devs push out some major overhauls, but I'm not holding my breath. Ring of Pain is the game you want.

I would give this a neutral review if that was a thing, because it was reasonably fun overall, but as other reviewers have all said, the balance is just atrocious. I won on the hardest difficulty with one character and don't really want to do it with all of them because it's not that interesting. I can *see* that at the higher difficulty the characters' inherent traits could potentially make it play differently, but in practice it would not, because the most effective way to play is to get the relic that makes attack items increase in power while held, and the relic that gets you a bomb each room, and then just do 200-400 damage to everything every time you enter a boss room. There's a couple of other relics that are similarly "if you get this you're probably gonna win" and then there's some just stupid relics like one that gives you +8 max health but deals you damage every turn. Even if you did manage to pair that with some kind of "reacts to damage" relic, the amount is too small to be useful and the fact of it being actively bad unless paired with something else just makes it a terrible pick. I selected it once just to see if its upgrade path made it turn into something good, but it did not. If this was a game in a void I would recommend it, but when there's Astrea and Alina of the Arena and Fights in Tight Spaces and Slay the Spire and etc. etc. there's not really a good reason to pick this one unless you've already exhausted the better-balanced options. The decision to make the main distinguishing features of the characters gated on playing it on hard (even though they're beneficial, so it would make sense to unlock the same features on easy!) is baffling.

For a roguelike game, it went for design philosophies which go against the spirit of roguelikes. Runs lack uniqueness between them, and characters when you unlock them have nothing unique to them, aside from stats. Do you want characters to have their signature traits unlocked ? You gotta make the game harder. How do you make the game harder ? You have to first unlock the equippable run modifier, by doing ACHIEVEMENTS (not completing runs like any other roguelike), unlocking them in the BESTIARY (which nothing in the game explains to you that it's where you unlock items and characters, because it's a misleading name for that menu), equipping them in your run modifier slots (which you unlock with your HIGH SCORE, not ACCUMULATED SCORE), sharing slots with things that modify your character and run in other ways, like by allowing you to even ACCESS your CHARACTER UNIQUE ITEMS... And ONLY THEN can your characters have ONE of their traits enabled. All that for your character choice to mean something. Other than that, it's items that you have to slot into your run modifier slots (which the game doesn't explain to you either, nor is the first one you start with slotted in the first place, or a default). Every single relic you get in game, are shared common relics (not to be confused with the rarity). Which, by the way, relics you get ? They take a limited amount of slots, instead of the standard of limitless relics with limits on weapons and the likes. But you still get a TON of relics. So, throughout the run, you have to get relics, get the currency to upgrade them, and once they're upgraded to the maximum level, get more of that in-game special currency (different from gold for shops) to turn them into passives, freeing up a slot. And while you go through that hassle, you obtain 2 more relics to upgrade and turn into passives, with even more currency to get. It's a tedious process, which has no place in a roguelike game. And then the game itself, where you need to attack enemies in a simple "Attack vs Defence" 1v1. You click on an enemy card to attack, you deal damage equals to your attack - their defence, and they deal damage back with the same calculation. But if you deal enough damage to kill them, they don't attack back. UNLESS they get the initiative modifier. HOWEVER there are cards dealing piercing damage, meaning that your defence means NOTHING. And those cards with piercing damage ? They start appearing towards the end of the first act, and by the end of the second act, half of the cards you fight deal piercing damage. At that point, why the hell would you level up your defence ? Only increase your attack, it's the only thing that matters. EXCEPT if you get enemies which take a limited amount of damage per attack, which can ALSO deal piercing damage. And after all of that ? You finish your run, not having completed it because it becomes absurd by the end, and you unlock nothing, because it's your 5th run and you ran out of easy-to-get achievements to unlock more content. This game is an afront to roguelike games. Go play Slay the Spire 2, or Megabonk, or Vampire Survivors, or even Across the Obelisk if you got friends willing to play that game with you. So many better options than this, that will make picking a character and playing runs mean something.

I recommend this game only if it has a really good discount. Otherwise, it's still an interesting experience, but a bit overpriced in my opinion. I think this game would benefit a lot from having a demo. Many players who love card Battler games would experience the core system mechanics and have enough to then commit to playing this one. This game became engaging once it "clicks". On my first run with the cat girl, I inspected the menu, the items, and, like you expect, I didn't understand anything. Quite normal, I think, I hopped in the adventure, and I mostly focused on understanding what was happening, what was important to focus on, what to avoid, what to level up, what was working, and what wasn't. I was learning how to survive and manage my resources. On my second run with my beloved overpowered Elf, she is not broken she has big potential, and I love her. I accidentally discovered a small exploit that helped me to understand some synergy and combination with the items. There are some surprisingly abusable strategies, some could be a means to the end. The game's difficulty can feel brutal, as some other review mentioned, Oh, I have the piercing damage, if you don't know how to make the right builds or combinations. These enemies are not jokes, but I was slaying cards like my elf was too powerful with that exploit, sustain, resist advance. I almost finished the game on my second run, but I miscalculated; I did the math wrong and got destroyed. I HAD A POTION, AAAAHHH. By the third run, the difficulty curve collapsed, and the game became easy, maybe too easy. I knew how to make the right build, I understood the potential. Oh my Elf, elves could be so scary, you know, my girl Frieren. I was overpowered even using a different build. I discovered another exploit or strategy. Unfortunately, this also reduced the replay tension. I finished the game, I was good, so I wanted to do the hard mode. Fourth run, even with the difficulty modifiers and the elite enemies, it felt repetitive, it felt more like a chore than a game. Finished it and even one hit some enemies. I loved the designs of the main characters. The enemies, however, could use a bit more personality and uniqueness; they have the style, just cook a bit more. Shark Gang and the Dragons were definitely a highlight for me! Loved them! Overall, this game has something to offer strong ideas, a very good and initially satisfying experiment. It requires balance tuning, replay variety, and polish, polish, polish. I think the soul of the game is somewhat solid. I think this is a good base for the developer and the team lunch a big update or be the base for an even better game. Making games is hard, even so, this is a game you can enjoy. --- Se supone que esta review iba a ser un par de líneas. En fin, un juego interesante de adquirir solo si tiene un buen descuento, además de que te guste este género. Conseguir ítems y levearlos para mejorar a tu personaje, combatir con enemigos y avanzar hacia la victoria. Buen juego, pero requiere cierta revisión y pulirlo para ser una gran experiencia. Gloria a mi elfita que me ayudó a pasar el juego.
